t1_DI.content:

| Exact page/article title | **Digging into decision intelligence** |
| Author(s) | **Not stated in the provided page content.** Cassie Kozyrkov, at Google, is identified as promoting the idea of decision intelligence and coining the term. |
| Publisher or journal | **Towards Data Science** |
| Publication year | **Year not stated** |
| Definition/treatment of decision intelligence and decision-making with analytics and AI | Decision intelligence, a term coined by Cassie Kozyrkov, aims to regroup known decision-making methods, insights, and best practices under a common umbrella, including analytics; frequentist and Bayesian statistics; machine learning; decision science; behavioral economics; and the psychology and neurology of decisions. It treats decision-making according to scale and readiness: machine learning for making decisions at scale, statistics for a small number of rigorous decisions, and analytics for situations where insight is needed before making a decision. |
| Boundary versus BI or data science | Data science is purposefully omitted from the listed decision-intelligence methods because it is described as a popular but not well-defined term; the post presents decision intelligence as an experiment to determine whether it better demarcates a coherent field of interest. The article describes decision intelligence as “defragmenting the current decision making landscape” and as encompassing both practical application and theoretical understanding of decision methods. |
t1_DI.description: Cassie Kozyrkov, at Google, promotes the term decision intelligence. This post distills a large number of Cassies's posts to dig in deeper.
t1_DI.author: Sanne de Roever

t3_APQC.title: APQC's Process Classification Framework® (PCF) Frequently Asked Questions
t3_APQC.content:
- **Title:** APQC's Process Classification Framework® (PCF) Frequently Asked Questions
- **Publisher:** APQC
- **Current PCF version:** Version 7.4
- **Publication/update year:** year not stated

- **PCF structure and use:** The PCF is a taxonomy and catalog, or index, of an organization’s process activities, organized to rationally capture, group, and decompose activities from a high-level process category to a process activity. Its elements include a hierarchy ID showing where an element sits among the other elements and a unique five-digit PCF element ID used for benchmarking, even when process element names and definitions change.
- **Versions:** APQC has a cross-industry version and industry-specific versions to better suit organizations; all versions are housed in APQC’s Resource Library.
- **Common process taxonomy:** The PCF creates a common language for organizations to communicate and define work processes comprehensively and without redundancies, and allows organizations to objectively track and compare performance internally and externally with organizations from any industry.
